clue.text: Heard youngsters prepared something to drink

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for youngsters is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a brood is a family of young, as of chicks

explanation.surface: Someone listens as the children make a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' signals a sound-alike: BROOD, a family of young, is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew tea or beer is to make a drink by steeping or fermenting, so this past tense matches 'prepared'.

clue.text: Ill-feeling Tommy expressed out loud

indicators.note: expressed out loud asks for the spoken form of the word for a Tommy

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier, one who serves in the ranks, a ranker

explanation.surface: A British soldier voices his resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the traditional nickname for a British private; a soldier in the ranks is a RANKER, which 'expressed out loud' turns into the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, lasting resentment, a strong form of hostility.

clue.text: Yarn by female writer

parts.note: wool is spun yarn used for knitting

explanation.surface: A story told by a woman author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a tale, but here it is knitting wool. Virginia Woolf was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf was a celebrated English novelist and essayist, so she is an example of an author.

clue.text: See WWII soldier go AWOL — despicable sort

parts.note: to go AWOL (absent without leave) is to desert
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A wartime soldier runs off and is branded a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division, which fought in North Africa in the Second World War; any member is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Britain's 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign were nicknamed after the jerboa on their badge.

clue.text: Pop idols met song writer

indicators.note: pop as a verb means burst, so the letters of the next words are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Pop stars meet a songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like the music genre, but it signals rearranging IDOLS MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodist composes tunes, so is a writer of songs.

clue.text: Film featured in very early edition of tabloid?

parts.note: midnight is the very earliest moment of a day
the Express is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A movie gets a mention in the first late-night run of a popular paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Midnight Express is a 1978 film about a prison escape; the Daily Express is a British tabloid, and a midnight edition would be a very early one.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is a 1978 Alan Parker prison drama, an example of a motion picture.

clue.text: Without resistance, woman gets overweight

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for woman goes around the other letter

parts.note: a lady is a woman
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A woman who stops resisting puts on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means 'outside': LADY goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy is a colloquial word for fat, as if full of lard.

clue.text: Society girl, with cries of pain, emerges into the open

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering high society
ouch is a cry of pain, so ouches are several such cries

explanation.surface: A debutante, yelping in pain, comes out into the daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'comes out' into society, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To debouch is to come out from a narrow place into open country, as a river or troops do.

clue.text: Plant type that is stored in glasses

indicators.note: stored in says the abbreviation for that is sits inside the word for glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A kind of plant is kept in spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a basic category in biological classification, so a kind of plant.

clue.text: Minor politician collared by Blair denies going astray

indicators.note: collared by says the politician is held inside the remade letters
going astray says the letters of the two words wander out of order

parts.note: CON is short for a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A Tory is seized by a former prime minister who keeps straying from the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a young person but is the definition. 'going astray' shuffles the eleven letters of the two names, and 'collared by' wraps them round the politician. Tony Blair was a British Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderable means small or unimportant, too slight to be worth considering.

clue.text: In London, perhaps, working class will show acceptance of rules

indicators.note: the two pieces given after the city word are placed in it

parts.note: London is one example of a city
on means working, as a machine that is switched on
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: In the capital, labourers show they obey the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is often called a form. 'In' at the front puts the two later pieces inside the city word, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformity is compliance with standards, rules or laws.

clue.text: Detachment of fool after university

indicators.note: after places the word for fool behind the university letter

parts.note: a nit is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool gets separated from his group after leaving college.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a group of soldiers sent off from a larger body, a military unit.

clue.text: Bowman showing greater cunning

definitions.meaning: a bowman shoots with bow and arrows
arch means sly or knowing, so the comparative means more cunning

explanation.definitionFit: A bowman is an archery marksman; arch means roguishly sly, and adding the comparative ending makes it more crafty.

clue.text: Tough guy routed Ireland in an hour

indicators.note: in places the remade letters inside the abbreviation for an hour

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: routed means put to flight in disorder, so the letters of the country are scattered

explanation.surface: A hard man defeated Ireland within sixty minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough guy' suggests a sporting hard man beating Ireland; 'routed' instead scatters the country's letters, which sit inside the hour abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner holds to an uncompromising policy, a tough and unbending person.

clue.text: Secret, soothing words to baby

definitions.meaning: something kept confidential, not to be revealed
words murmured to quieten a crying infant

explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush is informal for top secret; 'hush, hush' is also what a parent whispers to calm a child.

clue.text: Cricketer having settled score at length, say

parts.note: to square a debt or account is to settle the score, leaving all square
a leg is a single stretch of a journey or race, such as one length; say marks the example

explanation.surface: A cricket player who has evened up a grudge over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a fielding position in cricket, level with the batter on the leg side, and the fielder there is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, and the fielder standing there takes its name, so is an example of a cricketer.

clue.text: Means to do away with fish that's not quite putrefied

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: not quite means the word for putrefied is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: rotten means decayed or putrefied

explanation.surface: A way of getting rid of fish that is only nearly rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last N of ROTTEN. A garrotte is a wire or cord used to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotte is a strangling cord or wire, a means of killing someone.

clue.text: Golfer's error that put paid to albatross?

definitions.text: Golfer's error that put paid to albatross?

parts.words: Golfer's error that put paid to albatross?
parts.note: read as golf, a swing that misses the ball ruins any chance of an albatross (three under par); read literally, a bird in flight was shot down

explanation.surface: A golfer's mishit that cost him an albatross score.
explanation.walkthrough: An albatross in golf is three under par on a hole; it is also a large seabird, which a shot fired into the sky could kill.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the term means a stroke that misses the ball entirely, a mistake counted as a stroke.

clue.text: Indefinite amount held by moneylender, almost lacking security?

indicators.note: held by places the letter for an unspecified number inside the trimmed lender
almost removes the final letter of the moneylender word

parts.note: a usurer lends money at excessive interest
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A loan shark takes a vague sum, nearly without any collateral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims USURER to USURE; N, the algebraic 'any number', goes inside after U. 'Security' suggests loan collateral, but the definition means feeling secure.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unsure is to lack confidence or certainty, a lack of feeling secure.

clue.text: Put these in hair to create waves

definitions.meaning: curlers wound into hair to set it
long heavy waves rolling in from the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Hair rollers are cylinders for curling hair; rollers are also long swelling sea waves.

clue.text: Church abandons singing test

indicators.note: abandons means the church abbreviation leaves the word for singing

parts.note: choral means sung by a choir

explanation.surface: A church gives up its singing exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination.

clue.text: Mother takes part in weird play, so it seems

indicators.note: takes part in places the word for mother inside the remade letters
weird means strange, so the word play is twisted into a new order

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A mother acts in a bizarre drama, or so it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' scrambles the four letters of the drama word, and 'takes part in' sets the mother word inside them, after their first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently means as far as one can tell, seemingly.

clue.text: Chambers naturally will give some German translations

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The Chambers dictionary will supply a few German translations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' suggests the dictionary publisher, but here it means natural cavities in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra are natural cavities or sinuses in bone, so chambers formed by nature.

clue.text: Geordie friend in foreign location

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Tyneside, in the North East of England, NE
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A Newcastle mate is somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a person from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country, so a place abroad.

clue.text: Prince Charming's instruction for party game?

definitions.text: Prince Charming's instruction for party game?

parts.words: Prince Charming's instruction for party game?
parts.note: in the Cinderella story the prince orders a search for the owner of a glass shoe; the phrase is also a children's party game

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale prince sets the rules for a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt the slipper is a traditional party game; in Cinderella, Prince Charming searches the kingdom for the woman whose foot fits the glass slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a parlour game in which players pass a shoe around a circle while one tries to find it.

clue.text: Movie creating hostility among top actors

indicators.note: among says the word for hostility sits inside the word for leading performers

parts.note: stars are leading actors
war is open hostility

explanation.surface: A film causes feuding between its leading players.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's 1977 space-opera film, an example of a movie.

clue.text: A large fitting required for my shoe

indicators.note: fitting means set into, so the article and size letter go inside the exclamation

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh!
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone needs a big size of shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!', meaning GOSH; A and L go inside it after G.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a rubber overshoe worn to keep footwear dry.
